q: How do I calculate the carbon footprint of an RO water purifier?
title: RO water purifier footprint per unit
short: List the parts by weight: plastic body, membrane, filters, pump, adapter and tank, with supplier figures. Add the plant's moulding and assembly electricity per unit and packing. Use-phase electricity is a separate figure, stated with its assumptions.

ul: ABS or PP body and tank by weight.
RO membrane, sediment and carbon cartridges.
Booster pump, solenoid valve, adapter, PCB and UV lamp.
Moulding of the body, if done in house.
Carton, thermocol or moulded pulp inserts.

p: Report cradle to gate per unit. If a buyer wants use phase, state the daily litres, hours and years assumed.

example.title: Worked example: purifier assembly per unit (one month)
lines: Plant total: 21,300 / 20,000 = 1.065 kg CO2 per unit
Add plastics, membrane, filters and pump for the full figure
example.note: Inputs are illustrative; use your own bills and production records.

senseible: Senseible reads the plant's electricity bills (CEA grid factor 0.710 kg CO2 per kWh for FY 2024-25, CO2 Baseline Database version 21.0) and fuel invoices (IPCC 2006 defaults) into a fingerprinted Scope 1 and 2 record, the plant-level input to a per-unit figure. Bought-in materials go to the supplier evidence trail; product reports are self-declared drafts.
